text:
Mia: Quick sync — we need a concrete plan for next-quarter Dedicated roadmap: reserved-pool deprecation path, burst reconciliation for legacy customers, and an autoscale override story for high-priority tenants. Can folks weigh in with constraints and launch gates?
Sam: +1. main constraints: backward compatibility for contracts, billing alignment, and oncall complexity if we change eviction behavior.
Alex: Ops viewpoint — we can't change preemption semantics without a 2-week canary on a small pool. Also need metrics: preempt-rate, avg-latency impact, and failed-fallback-rate.
Jordan: CS: several pilot customers (two paying enterprise accounts) asked for guaranteed burst carryover for 6 months after downgrade. They want an SLA for burst availability during that window.
Taylor: Sales: those enterprises will push back hard if we remove carryover. We can offer a paid migration path. Suggest: offer a one-time buyout to convert leftover burst tokens to discounted reserved credits.
Priya: Legal: any carryover extension needs contract amendment. If we auto-prorate, include explicit language about token expiry and conversion.
Sam: Proposed technical policy (first pass):
```
policy_name: commit-taper-bridge
grace_period_days: 180  # legacy carryover window
carryover_behavior: soft -> throttled after 90 days -> disabled after 180 days
billing: prorate remaining tokens or convert at 2x discount to reserved credits
autoscale_override: tenant-level override allowed for 1 week after downgrade, max prewarm=2 nodes
```
Mia: Important to decide the grace_period and whether throttled means rate-limited or best-effort. Also need to pick gating KPIs for GA: <10% traffic failing fallback, <5% p50 latency regression, and no >2x spike in cost.
Alex: Throttled = rate-limited (token-bucket style). Implementation risk: we need a lightweight per-tenant bucket backed by redis; that's fine but needs infra PR and perf tests. Canary on 2 pools first.
Jordan: For customers, the 180d window is fine if we do one of: (a) migration credits, (b) a paid extension, or (c) automatic conversion to reserved at a predictable discount. Which of these is easiest to communicate?
Taylor: (c) automatic conversion is easiest to sell and avoids ad-hoc sales work. We should publish a simple example in the billing UI: "Your remaining burst tokens will convert to X reserved capacity".
Priya: Agree on conversion but require opt-out checkbox during downgrade. If we auto-convert, include refund/appeal process.
Sam: Autoscale override details: allow a tenant override when they have active migration ticket (CS-provided) — the override should be scoped to a labeled rollout and expire automatically in 7 days. Implementation sketch: add override flag in routing policy, evaluated before preemption.
Alex: Implementation notes: need changes in router (2 LOC) + policy store + UI toggle. Can ship backend-only then console follow-up. Oncall exposure: low if we gate to <5 tenants during canary.
Mia: Launch gating checklist draft:
- Contract language in place (Legal)
- Billing conversion UI text (Finance/Product)
- Canary plan + metrics (Eng/SRE)
- CS migration playbook + template emails (CS)
- Sales offer for paid extension (Sales)
If all green, soft-launch to pilot customers, then GA 30 days after no major regressions.
Jordan: I'll prepare the playbook and customer-facing FAQ. Need a single line describing customer impact for the downgrade email.
Taylor: I'll draft a sales offer (conversion discount options) and pricing language.
Priya: I'll provide contract addendum language by EOD Friday.
Sam: I'll open infra PRs (policy store + redis bucket) and a canary rollout plan. ETA 2w for backend, UI later.
Alex: I'll add monitoring dashboards and an alert if fallback failure rate >3% during canary.
deploy-bot: New canary plan created: canary/pool-bridge-171920 — assigned to Sam, Alex.
Mia: Great. Next sync Friday 10am to confirm PRs and legal text. Action items captured. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
